# HaruMusic 0.1.8

- Reduce Android first-audio buffering by requesting 128 KiB foreground media blocks; keep bounded read-ahead and cancellation, with the desktop cache retaining its 512 KiB default.
- Cap music source resolution at 6 seconds per provider and 12 seconds for the full chain. Stop repeating Netease quality requests after an account or risk-control rejection, preserve a valid highest-quality fallback, and show a short source failure reason.
- Match cross-platform MusicFree results against the native catalog item before resolving, preserving its native ID, hash, and available qualities; cache verified matches briefly to speed repeat playback.
- Keep album artwork prominent in the immersive Android player, raise the control cluster, and update the blurred artwork atmosphere from the audio clock at a low update rate to reduce unnecessary rendering work.

Validation: 139 automated tests, TypeScript checks, and Android embedded API smoke checks including the 128 KiB first-range assertion. The emulator has no outbound network, so live provider playback could not be verified there. Source access still depends on each provider's current catalog, account permissions, and CDN availability; no parser can guarantee every online track.

The bounded range scheduling approach was studied from [Salt Extend Online](https://github.com/YGHFv/Salt-Extend-Online). HaruMusic implements it independently for Fetch and HTML audio; it does not bundle the project's Java or BASS implementation.
